subject: History
description: Babur's victories, Humayun's struggles, Sher Shah Suri

questions.stem: BABUR, founder of the Mughal Empire in India, was descended from:
questions.explanation: BABUR (1483-1530) — born Zahir-ud-din Muhammad in Andijan (Fergana Valley, modern Uzbekistan). Father's lineage: TIMUR / Tamerlane (great-great-great grandfather). Mother's lineage: GENGHIS KHAN (descendant). Hence the name 'MUGHAL' (= Mongol). Started ruling Fergana at age 12 (1494), lost it, conquered Kabul (1504), then turned his eyes to India. Wrote BABURNAMA — autobiography in Chagatai Turkish (one of the world's earliest autobiographies, very candid + observant; on flora, fauna, customs of Hindustan).

questions.stem: Babur defeated Ibrahim Lodi at the FIRST BATTLE OF PANIPAT in:
questions.explanation: FIRST BATTLE OF PANIPAT — 21 April 1526. Babur (~12,000 troops) defeated Ibrahim Lodi (~100,000). Babur's tactical innovations: TULUGHMA (flank attacks); ARABA (cart-mounted CANNONS — first major battlefield use of artillery in India); MATCHLOCK MUSKETS. Won despite huge numerical disadvantage. Founded MUGHAL EMPIRE (lasted 1526-1857, ~331 years). 1527 — BATTLE OF KHANWA (vs Rana Sanga of Mewar — coalition of Rajputs). 1528 — Battle of Chanderi. 1529 — Battle of Ghaghra (vs Afghans). Died 1530 in Agra at 47.

questions.stem: HUMAYUN (Babur's son) was DEFEATED + EXILED by which Afghan ruler?

options.option_text: Daulat Khan Lodi, the Punjab governor
Sher Shah Suri (battles of Chausa + Kannauj)
Adil Shah, who was Hemu's master ruler

questions.explanation: HUMAYUN (r. 1530-40 + 1555-56) — Babur's son. Inherited unconsolidated empire. SHER SHAH SURI (Farid Khan, an Afghan from Bihar) — defeated Humayun at: BATTLE OF CHAUSA (1539, near Buxar — Humayun barely escaped, swam Ganga); BATTLE OF KANNAUJ (1540 — Humayun fled to Persia). Established SUR DYNASTY (1540-1555). HUMAYUN spent 15 YEARS in exile — Persia (Shah Tahmasp's court), then to Kabul + back. Returned 1555, briefly recaptured Delhi. Died 1556 (fell down stairs in his library). Son AKBAR (13) succeeded him → Mughals.

questions.stem: SHER SHAH SURI's most enduring administrative reform was:

options.option_text: Abolition of all kinds of property tax
Grand Trunk Road, revenue + currency reforms
Conversion of Hindus to Islam by force
Banning of Hindi as a court language

questions.explanation: SHER SHAH SURI (r. 1540-45) — short reign but enormous influence. Reforms: (1) GRAND TRUNK ROAD — rebuilt + extended ancient road from Sonargaon (Bengal) to Peshawar/Kabul (~2500 km). Sarais (rest houses) every ~25 km. (2) LAND REVENUE — measured land + fixed assessment based on yield (later refined by Akbar's Todar Mal — directly inspired by Sher Shah). (3) CURRENCY — introduced silver RUPEE (~178 grains; basis of modern Rupee) + copper DAM. (4) Improved postal system, taxation, judicial fairness. Died accidentally during siege of Kalinjar (gunpowder explosion). His MAUSOLEUM at Sasaram (Bihar) — magnificent.

questions.stem: Babur's most famous Indian CONQUEST included winning Battle of KHANWA (1527) against:
questions.explanation: BATTLE OF KHANWA (16 March 1527) — Babur (~5000) vs RANA SANGA / Sangram Singh of Mewar (~80,000 Rajput coalition, including ousted Lodi nobles). Rajputs hoped Babur would loot + return like Timur — but Babur intended to STAY. Babur's victory established Mughal rule. Used artillery + fortified camp. Distractor 1 = Panipat 1526 was vs Lodi. Distractor 3 = Krishnadeva Raya was south India, far from Mughal reach. Distractor 4 = anachronism (Babur was Humayun's father).

questions.stem: HUMAYUN's TOMB in Delhi (built by his widow Hamida Banu) was a:

options.option_text: First Mughal mausoleum (no garden tomb yet)
Architectural prototype for the Taj Mahal

questions.explanation: HUMAYUN's TOMB (Delhi) — built 1565-72 by his widow HAMIDA BANU BEGUM (Akbar's mother), designed by Persian architect MIRAK MIRZA GHIYAS. UNESCO WORLD HERITAGE SITE (1993). FIRST GARDEN-TOMB on the Indian subcontinent — set the template for Mughal tombs that followed: SIKANDRA (Akbar's), ITIMAD-UD-DAULAH (Nur Jahan's father), AURANGZEB's wife Bibi-ka-Maqbara, + most famously TAJ MAHAL (Shah Jahan, 1632-53). Architectural features: bulbous DOME, garden in CHARBAGH (4-quartered Persian style), red sandstone + white marble. Reverberated through Mughal architecture for 200 years.

questions.stem: After Humayun's death in 1556, the SECOND BATTLE OF PANIPAT was fought between Akbar's forces and:
questions.explanation: SECOND BATTLE OF PANIPAT (5 Nov 1556) — Akbar's forces (commanded by BAIRAM KHAN) vs HEMU CHANDRA (a Hindu general — born to a poor Brahmin family in Rewari, Haryana; rose through ranks to be Adil Shah Sur's wazir + general). Hemu had recaptured Delhi from Mughals after Humayun's death; declared himself 'VIKRAMADITYA' — a rare instance of a Hindu sovereign in Delhi between Prithviraj Chauhan + Marathas. He was hit by an arrow in the eye; captured + beheaded by Bairam Khan. Re-established Mughal control + ushered in 5 decades of Akbar's rule.
